statements.translation: The Shah — still a refugee in Rome — was able to return on 22 August 1953, at the invitation of the new head of government.

difference: English places surrender the day after the assault, French and German five days after the coup, and Hebrew on 19 August itself.
question: When did Mosaddegh surrender?

runs.note: English places surrender the day after the assault, French and German five days after the coup, and Hebrew on 19 August itself.

Hebrew states that Mosaddegh surrendered on 19 August 1953, English, Persian, and Arabic state that he surrendered the following day (20 August / 29 Mordad), and French and German state that he surrendered five days after the coup.

statements.quote: The following day, he surrendered himself at the Officers' Club, where General Zahedi had been set up with makeshift headquarters by the CIA.
Fünf Tage nach dem Putsch bot Mossadegh General Zahedi telefonisch seine Kapitulation an.
statements.translation: Five days after the coup, Mosaddegh offered his surrender to General Zahedi by telephone.

statements.quote: Cinq jours après le coup d'État, Mossadegh contacte le général Zahedi par téléphone pour se rendre.
statements.translation: Five days after the coup, Mosaddegh contacts General Zahedi by telephone to surrender.

statements.quote: ב-19 באוגוסט 1953 נכנע מוסאדק ונעצר על ידי הצבא, והשאה חזר לטהראן ושב לכס המלוכה, שבוע בלבד לאחר גירושו.
statements.translation: On 19 August 1953 Mosaddegh surrendered and was arrested by the army, and the Shah returned to Tehran and his throne, only a week after his expulsion.

statements.quote: در روز ۲۹ مرداد مصدق و بیشتر یارانش خود را به شهربانی تسلیم کردند.
statements.translation: On 29 Mordad [20 August], Mosaddegh and most of his associates surrendered themselves to the police.

statements.quote: في اليوم التالي ، استسلم إلى الجنرال زاهدي ، الذي كان من المقرر في الوقت نفسه مع وكالة الاستخبارات المركزية مع مقر مؤقت في نادي الضباط .
statements.translation: The next day, he surrendered to General Zahedi, who was at the same time set up with the CIA with a temporary headquarters at the Officers' Club.

question: How is the constitutional authority behind the Shah’s dismissal presented?

runs.note: English stresses the decrees’ legitimating function, while passages in German and French affirm constitutional authority and Persian records Mosaddegh’s denial of that authority. German, French and Persian also present competing legal interpretations, so none should be reduced to a single categorical position.

English treats the farmans as a CIA-distributed instrument of the coup's legitimacy; French and German give space to the argument that the Shah had a constitutional right of dismissal once parliament was dissolved; Persian presents Mosaddegh's opposing view at length (alongside Abbas Milani's counterpoint that Mosaddegh had earlier acknowledged such a right).

English and Arabic frame the Shah's dismissal power as stemming from the 1949 Constitutional Assembly held under martial law, whereas French, German, and Persian focus on the constitutional vacuum created by Mosaddegh's own dissolution of the Majlis in August 1953, noting that in the absence of parliament the constitution allowed the Shah to dismiss and appoint the prime minister.

statements.quote: These decrees, called Farmāns, played a major role in giving legitimacy to the coup, and were further spread by CIA officials.

Nach der Verfassung war der Schah berechtigt, den Premierminister nach der Auflösung des Parlaments, das den Premierminister gewählt hatte, abzusetzen und durch einen Interimspremierminister bis zur Neuwahl des Parlaments zu ersetzen.
statements.translation: Under the constitution, after dissolution of the parliament that had elected the prime minister, the Shah was entitled to remove him and replace him with an interim prime minister until new parliamentary elections.

statements.quote: Die Rechtslage bezüglich der politischen Befugnisse des Schahs war nach der Auflösung des Parlaments durch Mossadeghs Referendum vom 3. und 10. August wieder unklar.
statements.translation: After parliament’s dissolution through Mosaddegh’s referendum of 3 and 10 August, the legal position concerning the Shah’s political powers was once again unclear.

statements.quote: Les conditions légales requises pour un changement de gouvernement avaient été créées par Mossadegh lui-même avec la dissolution du Parlement.
statements.translation: Mosaddegh himself had created the legal conditions required for a change of government by dissolving Parliament.

statements.quote: محمد مصدق در دادگاه و کتاب خاطراتش عنوان می‌کند که مطابق با عرف و قانون اساسی و سابقه آن پادشاه اجازه عزل را ندارد و تنها می‌تواند در زمان رأی تمایل مجلس نسبت به صدور فرمان اقدام نماید که آن هم امری تشریفاتی است.
statements.translation: Mohammad Mosaddegh states in court and in his memoir that, according to custom, the constitution and precedent, the king has no authority to dismiss and may issue a decree only when parliament has expressed its preference, and that this too is ceremonial.

statements.quote: D'après la constitution (et pas selon l'habitude), le Chah avait le droit de destituer le Premier ministre après la dissolution du parlement qui avait élu le Premier ministre
statements.translation: According to the constitution (and not according to custom), the Shah had the right to dismiss the Prime Minister after the dissolution of the parliament that had elected him.

statements.quote: محمد مصدق در دادگاه و کتاب خاطراتش عنوان می‌کند که مطابق با عرف و قانون اساسی و سابقه آن پادشاه اجازه عزل را ندارد
statements.translation: In court and in his memoirs Mosaddegh states that, according to custom, the constitution and precedent, the king has no right of dismissal.

statements.quote: Die rechtlichen Voraussetzungen hierfür hatte Mossadegh mit der Auflösung des Parlaments selbst geschaffen.
statements.translation: Mossadegh himself had created the legal preconditions for this with the dissolution of parliament.

statements.quote: The Shah finally agreed to Mosaddegh's overthrow after Roosevelt said that the United States would proceed with or without him, and formally dismissed the prime minister in a written decree, an act that had been made part of the constitution during the Constitutional Assembly of 1949, convened under martial law, at which time the power of the monarchy was increased in various ways by the Shah himself.

وقبل أن يغادر وقع قرارين: الأول يعزل مصدق والثاني يعين الجنرال فضل الله زاهدي محله، وهو استغلال لجزء من الدستور خلال جمعية الدستور عام 1949 التي تعقد تحت الأحكام العرفية، في الوقت الذي تم زيادة قوة النظام الملكي بطرق مختلفة من قبل الشاه نفسه.
statements.translation: And before leaving he signed two decrees: the first dismissing Mosaddegh and the second appointing General Fazlollah Zahedi in his place, which was an exploitation of a part of the constitution during the Constitutional Assembly of 1949 held under martial law, at a time when the power of the monarchy was increased in various ways by the Shah himself.

statements.quote: Les conditions légales requises pour un changement de gouvernement avaient été créées par Mossadegh lui-même avec la dissolution du Parlement. D'après la constitution (et pas selon l'habitude), le Chah avait le droit de destituer le Premier ministre après la dissolution du parlement qui avait élu le Premier ministre
statements.translation: The legal conditions required for a change of government had been created by Mossadegh himself with the dissolution of Parliament. According to the constitution (and not according to custom), the Shah had the right to dismiss the Prime Minister after the dissolution of the parliament that had elected the Prime Minister

statements.quote: Auf Drängen der USA hatte der Schah nach langem Zögern am 13. August eingewilligt, per Dekret den früheren Innenminister im ersten Kabinett Mossadeghs General Fazlollah Zahedi zum neuen Premierminister zu ernennen. Die rechtlichen Voraussetzungen hierfür hatte Mossadegh mit der Auflösung des Parlaments selbst geschaffen. Nach der Verfassung war der Schah berechtigt, den Premierminister nach der Auflösung des Parlaments, das den Premierminister gewählt hatte, abzusetzen und durch einen Interimspremierminister bis zur Neuwahl des Parlaments zu ersetzen.
statements.translation: At the urging of the USA, the Shah after long hesitation agreed on 13 August to appoint by decree the former Interior Minister in Mossadegh's first cabinet, General Fazlollah Zahedi, as the new Prime Minister. Mossadegh had created the legal prerequisites for this himself with the dissolution of Parliament. According to the constitution, the Shah was entitled to depose the Prime Minister after the dissolution of the parliament that had elected the Prime Minister and replace him with an interim prime minister until the new election of parliament.

question: Who mobilised the crowds, and how much responsibility is assigned to foreign organisers?

runs.note: English explicitly describes both camps as paid, and Persian attributes payment of clerics, soldiers and street forces to Roosevelt’s account. French gives substantial room to domestic organisation and military defections, while Hebrew describes opposing demonstrators and army action without mentioning paid crowds.

English has Roosevelt paying both sides; Persian (quoting Roosevelt's account) says the crowd was paid yet adds that many were genuinely royalist and that wealthy citizens joined; French leaves open whether the Americans financed the final rising; Hebrew presents the clashes as a spontaneous popular confrontation without mention of payments.

English and Persian present Roosevelt’s payments, officers, and crowds as what made the second attempt work. French also records an account in which the American and British services had already left. German reports Takeyh’s view that foreign intelligence has been given too much weight and domestic anger too little.

statements.quote: Soon, massive popular protests, aided by Roosevelt's team, took place across the city and elsewhere with tribesmen at the ready to assist the coup, with anti- and pro-monarchy protesters, both being paid by Roosevelt.
بنابر کتاب «ضد کودتا» نوشته مأمور سیا کیم روزولت، او در این روز با خریدن فتوای برخی از روحانیون و همچنین دادن پول به ارتشیان، ولگردان و اوباش تهران آن‌ها را به خیابان‌ها کشانید.
statements.translation: According to Countercoup by CIA agent Kim Roosevelt, on this day he brought them into the streets by buying fatwas from some clerics and paying soldiers, vagrants and thugs in Tehran.

statements.quote: Vers midi, des unités policières et militaires désertent et rejoignent les opposants à Mossadegh et prennent d'assaut le département d'État, la préfecture de police et le quartier général de l'état-major de l'armée.
statements.translation: Around noon, police and military units desert, join Mosaddegh’s opponents, and storm the State Department, police headquarters and army general staff headquarters.

statements.quote: מפגינים בעד ונגד השאה יצאו לרחובות, ובתוך ימים נהרגו במהומות כשלוש מאות איש.
statements.translation: Demonstrators for and against the Shah took to the streets, and within days about three hundred people were killed in the riots.

statements.quote: اگر چه احتمالاً اغلب‌شان سرشار از احساساتِ سلطنت‌طلبانه بودند اما به روشنی برای این کار پول گرفته بودند؛ بین آن‌ها انبوهی آدمِ بیکار و بسیاری اوباش و الواتِ سرشناس بودند.
statements.translation: Although most of them were probably full of royalist sentiment, they had clearly been paid for this; among them were masses of unemployed men and many well-known thugs and ruffians.

statements.quote: Quoi qu'il en soit, aidé ou non financièrement par les Américains, Zahedi utilise ses réseaux pour déclencher des manifestations en sa faveur et celle du Chah.
statements.section: Contre-coup d'État et retournement de situation
statements.translation: In any case, financially aided by the Americans or not, Zahedi uses his networks to trigger demonstrations in his favour and that of the Shah.

statements.quote: איראן נכנסה למערבולת פנימית. מפגינים בעד ונגד השאה יצאו לרחובות, ובתוך ימים נהרגו במהומות כשלוש מאות איש.
statements.translation: Iran entered an internal turmoil. Demonstrators for and against the Shah took to the streets, and within days about three hundred people were killed in the riots.

statements.quote: By paying mobs to demonstrate, tricking Mosaddegh into urging his supporters to stay home, and bribing and mobilising officers against Mosaddegh, he was able to force a military confrontation outside Mosaddegh's home.

Selon d'autres sources, comme la biographie du Chah d'Yves Bomati et Houchang Nahavandi, les Américains (et les Britanniques) se seraient retirés du projet et n'auraient pas participé à la prise de pouvoir finale.
statements.section: Contre-coup d'État et retournement de situation
statements.translation: According to other sources, such as Yves Bomati and Houchang Nahavandi’s biography of the Shah, the Americans and British reportedly withdrew from the project and did not participate in the final seizure of power.

statements.quote: Eine dem gängigen Geschichtsbild widersprechende Interpretation des Sturzes von Mossadegh vertritt der Iran-Experte Ray Takeyh. Laut ihm wurde die Rolle der westlichen Geheimdienste bei diesem Ereignis bisher überschätzt und die wegen der wirtschaftlichen Entwicklung zunehmende Stimmung gegen Mossadegh in der iranischen Mittelschicht und im Klerus zu wenig berücksichtigt.
statements.translation: Iran expert Ray Takeyh advances an interpretation of Mosaddegh’s overthrow that contradicts the prevailing account. According to him, Western intelligence services’ role has been overestimated, while growing opposition among Iran’s middle class and clergy arising from economic developments has received too little consideration.

question: How many deaths and injuries are reported in the overthrow?

runs.note: Persian gives an attributed figure of 41 killed and 75 injured; English and Arabic give nearly 300 deaths, while French and German give over 200 deaths and 300 injuries mainly outside the house. These figures have different stated scopes, especially Hebrew’s approximately 300 deaths over several days, and are not all explicit totals for 19 August alone.

The Persian version, citing a forensic official, reports 41 killed and 75 wounded, while the English, Arabic, French, German and Hebrew versions report roughly 200-300 dead (fr/de add 300 wounded); the very short Russian, Spanish and Turkish versions give no figures.

The Persian version, citing the forensic medicine chief, gives 41 killed and 75 wounded, while English, Arabic and Hebrew say around 300 dead and French and German say over 200 dead plus 300 wounded. The short Russian, Spanish and Turkish versions give no figure.

English, Arabic, and Hebrew state that around 300 people were killed, French and German state that over 200 were killed and 300 wounded (primarily in front of Mosaddegh's house), and Persian cites the head of the Forensic Medicine Organization to report 41 killed and 75 injured.

English, Arabic, and Hebrew give about 300 dead. French and German give more than 200 dead and 300 wounded. Persian cites a forensic figure of 41 dead and 75 wounded. Russian, Spanish, and Turkish give no toll.

statements.quote: بنا به نوشته سعید حکمت رئیس اداره پزشکی قانونی در جریان این کودتا ۴۱ تن مقتول و ۷۵ تن مجروح شدند.
statements.translation: According to Saeed Hekmat, head of the forensic medicine department, 41 people were killed and 75 injured during this coup.

statements.quote: The protests turned increasingly violent, leaving almost 300 dead, at which point the pro-monarchy leadership, led by retired army General and former Minister of Interior in Mosaddegh's cabinet, Fazlollah Zahedi, interceded, joined with underground figures such as the Rashidian brothers and local strongman Shaban Jafari.
وحدثت اشتباكات بعنف في الشوارع ونهب و حرقت المساجد و الصحف وخلفت ما يقرب من 300 قتيلا .
statements.translation: Violent clashes occurred in the streets, with looting and the burning of mosques and newspapers, leaving nearly 300 dead.

statements.quote: Les affrontements armés entre les partisans de Mossadegh et les forces de Zahedi se déroulent principalement devant la maison de Mossadegh, faisant plus de 200 morts et 300 blessés.
statements.translation: Armed clashes between Mosaddegh’s supporters and Zahedi’s forces take place mainly outside Mosaddegh’s house, leaving more than 200 dead and 300 wounded.

statements.quote: Die bewaffneten Auseinandersetzungen zwischen Mossadegh-Anhängern und Zahedi-Truppen fanden überwiegend vor dem Hause Mossadeghs statt und forderten über 200 Tote und 300 Verwundete.
statements.translation: Armed clashes between Mosaddegh supporters and Zahedi’s troops took place mainly outside Mosaddegh’s house and claimed more than 200 dead and 300 wounded.

statements.quote: מפגינים בעד ונגד השאה יצאו לרחובות, ובתוך ימים נהרגו במהומות כשלוש מאות איש.
statements.translation: Demonstrators for and against the Shah took to the streets, and within days about three hundred people were killed in the riots.

statements.quote: The protests turned increasingly violent, leaving almost 300 dead
ובתוך ימים נהרגו במהומות כשלוש מאות איש.
statements.translation: And within days some three hundred people were killed in the riots.

statements.quote: После свержения Мосаддык был осуждён за государственную измену и приговорён к трём годам тюремного заключения
statements.translation: (The very short Russian version gives no casualty figure for the coup.)

statements.quote: El 21 de diciembre de 1953, Mosaddeq entró a pasar a tres años de reclusión en aislamiento en una prisión militar
statements.translation: (The very short Spanish version gives no casualty figure for the coup.)

statements.quote: Darbenin ardından vatana ihanetle yargılanarak üç yıl hücre hapsine mahkûm edilmiş
statements.translation: (The very short Turkish version gives no casualty figure for the coup.)

statements.quote: وحدثت اشتباكات بعنف في الشوارع ونهب و حرقت المساجد و الصحف وخلفت ما يقرب من 300 قتيلا
statements.translation: Violent clashes, looting and burning of mosques and newspapers occurred, leaving nearly 300 dead.

statements.quote: faisant plus de 200 morts et 300 blessés
statements.translation: leaving more than 200 dead and 300 wounded

statements.quote: forderten über 200 Tote und 300 Verwundete

groups.answer: Sentenced to death, reduced to prison
Three years, less than death penalty

difference: English distinguishes a requested death sentence from the three-year sentence imposed, and Persian describes acquittal on capital charges followed by conviction for disobedience. Arabic, German and French instead describe a death sentence being reduced, with different accounts of who secured the reduction; English and French also give different December dates.
question: Was Mosaddegh sentenced directly to imprisonment, acquitted of capital charges, or sentenced to death and reprieved?

runs.note: English distinguishes a requested death sentence from the three-year sentence imposed, and Persian describes acquittal on capital charges followed by conviction for disobedience. Arabic, German and French instead describe a death sentence being reduced, with different accounts of who secured the reduction; English and French also give different December dates.

Arabic, French and German say a death sentence was handed down and then commuted (by the Shah's intervention or the prosecution's request), while English, Persian, Hebrew (and the short Russian and Spanish versions) say he was directly sentenced to three years, with prosecutors having sought death.

English, Persian, and Spanish state that the court sentenced Mosaddegh to three years' solitary confinement (with Persian noting he was acquitted of the capital charges and English/Spanish noting prosecutors had sought death), whereas Arabic, French, and German state that the tribunal sentenced him to death and the sentence was then commuted to three years (by the Shah's intervention in French and German).

English says prosecutors asked for death but the court gave three years. Persian says he was acquitted of the capital charges and sentenced to three years for disobeying the Shah. French and German say a death sentence was commuted by the Shah. Arabic says a death sentence was later reduced, and attributes the reduction to the prosecution. The hearing date is 21 December in English and 22 December in French; Arabic places the trial on 21 September 1953.

statements.quote: On 21 December 1953, Mosaddegh was sentenced to three years' solitary confinement in a military prison, well short of the death sentence requested by prosecutors.
دادگاه اگرچه او را از اتهامات مهمی چون اقدام علیه اساس سلطنت و کودتا علیه قانون اساسی که حکم اعدام داشت، تبرئه کرد ولی به جهت تمرد از فرمان شاه او را به سه سال زندان محکوم کرد.
statements.section: محاکمه و زندان و خانه نشینی
statements.translation: Although the court acquitted him of major charges such as acting against the foundations of the monarchy and a coup against the constitution, which carried the death penalty, it sentenced him to three years in prison for disobeying the Shah’s order.

statements.quote: حَكَمَ نظام الشاه على الدكتور مصدق بالإعدام، ثم خفف الحكم لاحقاً إلى سجن انفرادي لثلاث سنوات في الحبس الانفرادي، وقد خففت عقوبة الإعدام بعد طلب من النيابة العامة.
statements.translation: The Shah’s regime sentenced Dr Mosaddegh to death, then reduced the sentence to three years in solitary confinement; the death penalty was reduced at the prosecution’s request.

statements.quote: Mossadegh wurde von dem Militärtribunal zum Tode verurteilt. Durch eine Intervention des Schahs wurde die Strafe auf drei Jahre Gefängnis reduziert.
statements.section: Der Prozess und die letzten Jahre
statements.translation: Mosaddegh was sentenced to death by the military tribunal. Through an intervention by the Shah, the sentence was reduced to three years in prison.

statements.quote: Le 22 décembre 1953 Mohammad Mossadegh est condamné à mort mais la grâce du Chah fait commuer sa peine en trois ans d’emprisonnement.
statements.section: Procès, condamnation, assignation à résidence et fin de vie
statements.translation: On 22 December 1953 Mohammad Mossadegh is sentenced to death, but the Shah’s pardon commutes his sentence to three years’ imprisonment.

statements.quote: با توجه به تبرئه او از اتهامات اصلی چون «تلاش برای برهم زدن اساس سلطنت» و «کودتا علیه قانون اساسی» به سه سال حبس مجرد (انفرادی) محکوم شد.
statements.section: محاکمه و زندان و خانه نشینی
statements.translation: Having been acquitted of the main charges such as 'attempting to overthrow the monarchy' and 'coup against the constitution', he was sentenced to three years of solitary confinement.

statements.quote: מוסאדק נשפט בעוון בגידה ונדון לשלוש שנות מאסר.
statements.translation: Mosaddegh was tried for treason and sentenced to three years in prison.

statements.quote: El 21 de diciembre de 1953, Mosaddeq entró a pasar a tres años de reclusión en aislamiento en una prisión militar, muy por debajo de la sentencia de muerte impuesta por los fiscales.
statements.translation: On 21 December 1953, Mosaddeq entered to spend three years of solitary confinement in a military prison, well below the death sentence imposed by the prosecutors.

statements.quote: محمد مصدق را پس از کودتای ۲۸ مرداد در دادگاه نظامی محاکمه و با توجه به تبرئه او از اتهامات اصلی چون «تلاش برای برهم زدن اساس سلطنت» و «کودتا علیه قانون اساسی» به سه سال حبس مجرد (انفرادی) محکوم شد.
statements.section: محاکمه و زندان و خانه نشینی
statements.translation: After the 28 Mordad coup Mosaddegh was tried in a military court and, having been acquitted of the main charges such as trying to overthrow the monarchy and a coup against the constitution, was sentenced to three years’ solitary confinement.

difference: English gives March, Spanish 20 March and Arabic 1 May for Mosaddegh’s nationalisation action; German explicitly locates the legislative enactment on 15 March under Ala. The versions differ in chronology and allocation of credit, while also describing different stages of legislation and implementation.
question: When was oil nationalisation enacted, and who receives credit for the legislative step?

runs.note: English gives March, Spanish 20 March and Arabic 1 May for Mosaddegh’s nationalisation action; German explicitly locates the legislative enactment on 15 March under Ala. The versions differ in chronology and allocation of credit, while also describing different stages of legislation and implementation.

statements.quote: In March 1951, Mosaddegh nationalised the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company, cancelling its oil concession, which was otherwise set to expire in 1993, and expropriating its assets.
وفي 1 مايو أي بعد يومين من استلامه السلطة قام مصدق بتأميم النفط الإيراني وألغى الامتياز الممنوح لشركة النفط الإيراني البريطاني الذي ينتهي سنة 1993 وقام بمصادرة أصولها.
statements.translation: On 1 May, described as two days after taking power, Mosaddegh nationalised Iranian oil, cancelled the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company’s concession due to expire in 1993, and confiscated its assets.

statements.quote: Una de sus primeras medidas fue decretar la nacionalización de la Anglo-Persian Oil Company el 20 de marzo de 1951, aprobada por la mayoría parlamentaria y ratificada cinco días después por el Senado.
statements.translation: One of his first measures was to decree nationalisation of the Anglo-Persian Oil Company on 20 March 1951, approved by the parliamentary majority and ratified five days later by the Senate.

statements.quote: Eine Woche nach der Ermordung Razmaras verabschiedete unter Premierminister Hossein Ala das Parlament am 15. März 1951 das Gesetz zur Verstaatlichung der Ölindustrie.
statements.section: Verstaatlichung der Ölindustrie unter Premierminister Hossein Ala
statements.translation: One week after Razmara’s assassination, under Prime Minister Hossein Ala, parliament passed the law nationalising the oil industry on 15 March 1951.

question: What casualty figures are given for the July 1952 demonstrations?

runs.note: English combines deaths and serious injuries in its figure above 250, whereas Arabic makes above 250 the number killed and adds injuries separately. French and German give 36 deaths in their account of the Tehran demonstration on 21 July, a narrower geographical and temporal scope.

English states that over 250 demonstrators across five cities were killed or seriously injured, whereas Arabic translates this as over 250 killed in those cities plus many injured; French and German state that 36 people were killed in Tehran on 21 July, and Persian simply says 'several people' were killed.

question: Why did Mosaddegh halt the 1952 parliamentary (17th Majlis) elections before all seats were filled?

runs.note: Only the English, Persian, and Arabic versions discuss the halting of the 1952 parliamentary elections; all three present both the explanation of interference (by British-funded agents in English and Arabic, or by the army and royal court in Persian) and the historian's view (Abrahamian) that Mosaddegh stopped voting once a quorum of 79 (or 80 in Persian) was reached to prevent the opposition from winning the provincial seats. Even the long French and German versions omit this episode.

statements.quote: According to historian Ervand Abrahamian: "Realizing that the opposition would take the vast majority of the provincial seats, Mosaddegh stopped the voting as soon as 79 deputies—just enough to form a parliamentary quorum—had been elected." An alternative account is offered by journalist Stephen Kinzer: Beginning in the early 1950s under the guidance of C.M. Woodhouse, chief of the British intelligence station in Tehran, Britain's covert operations network had funnelled roughly £10,000 per month to the Rashidian brothers (two of Iran's most influential royalists) in the hope of buying off, according to CIA estimates, "the armed forces, the Majlis (Iranian parliament), religious leaders, the press, street gangs, politicians and other influential figures". Thus, in his statement asserting electoral manipulation by "foreign agents", Mosaddegh suspended the elections.

کار بجایی رسید که پس از انتخاب ۸۰ نماینده، مصدق به دلیل دخالت ارتش و دربار، مجبور شد دستور توقف انتخابات حوزه‌های باقی‌مانده را صادر کند. ولی برخی مورخان عقیده دارند مصدق با پی بردن به اینکه جناح مخالف، اکثریت قابل توجه کرسی‌های استانی را به‌دست خواهند آورد، پس از اینکه انتخاب شوندگان به حد نصاب رسیدند (هفتاد و نه نماینده)، انتخابات را متوقف کرد.

statements.translation: Matters reached a point where after the election of 80 deputies, Mosaddegh, due to the interference of the army and the court, was forced to issue an order halting the elections in the remaining constituencies. However, some historians believe that Mosaddegh, realizing that the opposition faction would gain a significant majority of provincial seats, stopped the elections after those elected reached a quorum (seventy-nine deputies).

statements.quote: وبالتالي فقد أكد مصدق في بيانه أن هناك تلاعبا انتخابيا يديره "عملاء أجانب" فعلق بذلك الإنتخابات. ولم يعترض أحدا على البيان، لذا فقد تأجلت الانتخابات إلى أجل غير مسمى. ووفقا لإرفاند إبراهيميان: "نحن ندرك أن المعارضة تريد أخذ الغالبية العظمى من مقاعد الأقاليم، فقد أوقف مصدق التصويت عندما انتخب 79 نائبا وهو يكفي لتشكيل النصاب البرلماني".
statements.translation: Consequently, Mosaddegh confirmed in his statement that there was electoral manipulation run by 'foreign agents' and thus suspended the elections. No one objected to the statement, so the elections were postponed indefinitely. And according to Ervand Abrahamian: 'Realizing that the opposition would take the vast majority of the provincial seats, Mosaddegh stopped the voting when 79 deputies were elected, which was enough to form the parliamentary quorum.'

question: Did Mosaddegh pass a strike-ban law in October 1952 that reversed the presumption of innocence and led to building ten new prisons?

runs.note: The French and German versions state that on 21 October 1952 Mosaddegh signed a law banning all strikes, presuming arrested strike organizers guilty until proven innocent, and prioritizing the construction of ten new prisons as jails filled up—an account absent from all other versions, including the long English and Persian articles.

statements.quote: Le 21 octobre 1952, Mossadegh avait signé une loi promulguant une loi interdisant toute grève et autorisant la police à arrêter les personnes organisant des grèves. Toute personne arrêtée devrait être immédiatement reconnue coupable, tant qu'elle ne pourrait pas prouver le contraire, une loi inacceptable pour Baghai. Les prisons iraniennes se remplirent rapidement, forçant Mossadegh à faire de la construction de dix nouvelles prisons une priorité.
statements.translation: On 21 October 1952, Mossadegh had signed a law enacting a ban on all strikes and authorizing the police to arrest people organizing strikes. Anyone arrested was to be immediately deemed guilty so long as they could not prove the contrary, a law unacceptable to Baghai. Iranian prisons filled rapidly, forcing Mossadegh to make the construction of ten new prisons a priority.

statements.quote: Mossadegh hatte am 21. Oktober 1952 mit seiner Unterschrift ein Gesetz in Kraft gesetzt, das jeden Streik verbot und es der Polizei erlaubte, Personen, die Streiks organisierten, festzunehmen. Dabei sollte jeder Festgenommene unmittelbar als schuldig gelten, solange er nicht das Gegenteil beweisen konnte. Dieses Gesetz war für Baqa’i unannehmbar. Die Gefängnisse im Iran füllten sich rasch, so dass sich Mossadegh gezwungen sah, mit höchster Priorität zehn neue Gefängnisse bauen zu lassen.
statements.translation: On 21 October 1952, Mossadegh had put into force with his signature a law that banned every strike and allowed the police to arrest persons who organized strikes. Every arrested person was to be considered immediately guilty as long as they could not prove the opposite. This law was unacceptable to Baqa'i. The prisons in Iran filled up rapidly, so that Mossadegh was forced to have ten new prisons built with the highest priority.

question: Did Mosaddegh dissolve parliament before or after the failed mid-August attempt?

statements.quote: On 16 August, after an initial failed coup attempt by the CIA,the Parliament was suspended indefinitely, and Mosaddegh's emergency powers were extended.
در ۲۱ مرداد ۱۳۳۲ مصدق، رسماً نتیجه یعنی «ابقای دولت و انحلال مجلس ۱۷» را اعلام کرده و از شاه خواست فرمان برگزاری انتخابات جدید را امضا کند؛ ولی او این رفراندوم را تأیید نکرد.
statements.translation: On 21 Mordad 1332 Mosaddegh formally announced the result, keeping the government and dissolving the 17th Majlis, and asked the Shah to sign an order for new elections; the Shah did not confirm the referendum.

statements.quote: در ۲۳ مردادماه ۱۳۳۲ بنا بر نقشه سیا موسوم به تی پی آژاکس برای براندازی دولت مصدق، شاه طی دو حکم جداگانه، فرمان عزل مصدق و نخست‌وزیری تیمسار زاهدی را امضا می‌کند.
statements.translation: On 23 Mordad 1332, under the CIA plan called TPAJAX to overthrow Mosaddegh’s government, the Shah signed two separate orders, dismissing Mosaddegh and naming General Zahedi prime minister.

statements.quote: Jenen, die Mossadegh vorhielten, dass er nach der Auflösung des Parlaments aufgrund des Referendums vom 3. bzw. 10. August eine Verfassungskrise ausgelöst hätte und deshalb der Schah das verfassungsmäßige Recht gehabt hätte, ihn zu entlassen und einen neuen Premierminister zu ernennen, entgegnete Mossadegh, dass das Dekret seiner Entlassung das Datum vom 22 Mordad (13. August) trage, während das Parlament erst durch eine Zeitungsnotiz vom 25 Mordad (16. August) aufgelöst worden sei.
statements.translation: To those who said that after dissolving parliament by the referendum of 3 or 10 August he had caused a constitutional crisis, so the Shah had the right to dismiss him, Mosaddegh replied that the dismissal decree was dated 22 Mordad (13 August), while parliament was dissolved only by a newspaper notice of 25 Mordad (16 August).
